question: Should Telegram expose standalone `pin` and `unpin` message-tool actions, and what gate plus target semantics should protect them?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature changes persistent Telegram chat state through privileged bot credentials and the current config surface has no approved pin-specific gate or implicit-unpin contract.

options.title: Approve gated explicit actions
options.body: Add Telegram-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete message id unless maintainers approve an implicit unpin mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Keep delivery pin only
options.body: Keep the existing delivery-pin capability for messages OpenClaw just sent and do not expose standalone pin/unpin mutations yet.

options.title: Request a design note first
options.body: Ask for a short design covering bot admin expectations, per-account gating, implicit unpin behavior, and forum-topic semantics before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve gated explicit actions
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-owned `pin` and `unpin` actions behind an explicit action gate, require a concrete message id unless maintainers approve an implicit unpin mode, and require live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram action/runtime history and plugin-boundary work make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
